text:
Jackson Blake was a fourth-round pick, 109th overall, and at 23 he is one of the most effective five-on-five forwards in the league. He put together an 11-game, 13-point streak earlier this month (RotoWire), and Dimitri Filipovic devoted a PDOcast episode to "Jackson Blake being an absolute dog this season." With 23 points in 24 games and 82% of Carolina's power-play time (40% last season), this is a breakout by every measure.

The best part is that the process is ahead of the results. Carolina takes 68% of the expected goals (chance quality) at five on five with him on, 11 points better than without him, and he has 7 goals on 10.0 expected. That means he's getting better looks than his goals show. His teammates have converted at a hot rate (5.7 goals above expected with him on), which balances it some. Evolving-Hockey noted last season that he plays with strong teammates (96th percentile), which flatters on-ice numbers. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put his scoring chances from the slot in the 88th percentile. Yahoo Sports already put one feat of his "in Connor McDavid Company"; the goals are the part still lagging behind.
headline: Jackson Blake's breakout is for real
